answer: The protocol issues dynamic opportunity-cost bonds backed by a zero-knowledge verifiable delay, locking each identity to a quartz stake proportional to marginal capital cost. A subgame-perfect punishment matrix slashes any agent that attempts to forge extra identities by an amount exceeding the ridge of the attacker's discounted revenue, yielding strictly negative expected utility. Consequently the unique Nash equilibrium converges to honest participation as rational agents internalize the collateral lock-up, eliminating profitable deviation.
